facts.text: Québec City ranks second only to Toronto in insurance and financial services; four of Canada's ten largest life and health insurers are based here and the sector is 17.9% of city GDP.
The Québec City region has more than 120 life sciences businesses and some 80 research centres, and is home to nearly 64,000 workers with life sciences degrees.
The Québec City CMA's unemployment rate stands at 3% at the start of 2026, a rare milestone in the past decade.
Québec City is home to the National Assembly, and its leading industries include life sciences, food and nutrition, green building, insurance and financial services, ICT and optics-photonics.

overview: Quebec City had 549,459 residents in the 2021 Census, up 3.3% from 531,902 in 2016. Its 265,711 occupied dwellings are spread over 452.3 square kilometres, and the median household income in 2020 was $70,500.

As the provincial capital, the city relies on government, insurance and financial services, life sciences and tourism, and unemployment is very low. A local business sells to a stable, overwhelmingly French-speaking market with steady public-sector incomes.
